- **Data classes, and a web session that holds nothing private beyond its admitted prompt (#244; slice R1a of #152).** Every capability manifest states `provides.dataClass`: `fixture`, `presence` and the new `web` capability are `public`; `flair`, `discord`, `anchored-edit`, `work`, `reachy`, `observatory`, `tps-mail` and the planned `mail` are `private`, and a manifest without a class counts as private. A session that holds `web`, or allows a web tool, is refused when it would also hold a private-class capability, any pi built-in tool, a tool or extension bob cannot attribute, `soul.md` content, the persistent runtime's standing contract, a context file, skill, prompt template or custom system prompt, restored history (including history from a session that held a private capability), or a system prompt other than bob's reviewed web prompt. Each check names, in one error, every problem that check can see: the check at `bob.yaml` load sees only the capability set (after each capability block passes its schema), and the session factory sees the rest. The refusal says whether the web capability, an allowed egress tool or both made it a web session, and names the matching remedy. pi's own prompt template names local paths, so a web session sends bob's reviewed prompt instead and has no agent workspace (pi's working directory is `/`), and the prompt pi assembles is compared with the reviewed one. The admitted one-shot task is allowed, and the system prompt carries a capped copy of it; it is not classified by this rule. The rule is checked when `bob.yaml`'s capabilities are resolved, by the session factory before it builds pi's runtime, and on the composed session at creation, after the mode binds extensions and after every reload; there is no override. bob's post-compaction "what remains" note is not sent into a web session. The `web` capability ships its manifest, catalog entry, extension and a flat config block (`allow_http`, `fetch_max_chars`, `fetch_per_turn`, `text_per_turn`), validated when `bob.yaml` is loaded and again when the extension reads `BOB_CAP_WEB`; it registers no tool and has no network code. `web_fetch` and `web_search` are classified `egress`: a resident agent's policy excludes them unless its role sets `tools.allowResidentWeb: true`, which removes only that resident egress exclusion (an explicit `tools.exclude` entry still wins; `allowResidentShell` does not cover them), and the mail-turn allowlist does not include them. The `jarvis` and `ea` roles list both tools and grant `allowResidentWeb`; the composition rule still refuses web beside Flair or Discord. `bob doctor` warns when a resident agent's allowlist names a web tool that is dropped while the resident web grant is absent, and then also says to remove the tool from `tools.exclude` if it is listed there; an exclusion alone, with the grant in effect, does not trigger this warning. (`test/shell/data-class.test.ts`, `test/shell/web-composition-session.test.ts`, `test/shell/web-policy.test.ts`, `test/shell/web-note.test.ts`, `test/capabilities/web/config.test.ts`)
